territorial_scope.description: Applies to filings presented to the Municipal Criminal Court of the City of Tulsa.

evidence.quote: must disclose in that filing that generative AI was used

summary.short: Tulsa Municipal Criminal Court rule requiring any attorney, pro se defendant, victim or other party who uses generative AI in preparing a filing to disclose that use in the filing and name the specific tool. Filings remain subject to 12 O.S. §2011 certification.
summary.long: The rule applies to documents filed with the Tulsa Municipal Criminal Court. Any attorney, pro se defendant, victim or other party that uses a generative AI tool in preparing or drafting a filing must disclose in that filing that generative AI was used, and must state the name of the specific tool. Generative AI is stated to include, but not be limited to, ChatGPT, Bing AI and Google Bard. The rule states that 12 O.S. §2011 continues to apply to all filings. The court will construe filings, as certified by the person signing them, to comply with 12 O.S. §2011(B)(2). The text gives no effective date and states no penalty or other enforcement measure for non-disclosure.

relations.note: The text says 12 O.S. §2011 continues to apply to all filings with the Municipal Criminal Court. It also says the court will construe filings, as certified by the signer, to comply with 12 O.S. §2011(B)(2). The target is not in the registry.

evidence.quote: All filers should note that 12 O.S. §2011 continues to apply to all filings presented to the Municipal Criminal Court.
